At any junction, Kirchhoff's Current Law says that the total current entering the junction is equal to the total current leaving it.

For the first junction, $5\text{A}$ enters. The currents leaving are $1\text{A}$ and $I_{1}$ .

So,

$5=1+I_{1}$

$\Rightarrow I_{1}=5-1=4\text{A}$

For the second junction, $I_{1}$ enters. The currents leaving are $1.5\text{A}$ and $I_{2}$ .

So,

$I_{1}=1.5+I_{2}$

Putting $I_{1}=4\text{A}$ ,

$4=1.5+I_{2}$

$\Rightarrow I_{2}=4-1.5=2.5\text{A}$

For the third junction, $I_{2}$ enters. The currents leaving are $1.5\text{A}$ and $I_{3}$ .

So,

$I_{2}=1.5+I_{3}$

Putting $I_{2}=2.5\text{A}$ ,

$2.5=1.5+I_{3}$

$\Rightarrow I_{3}=2.5-1.5=1\text{A}$

The values of $I_{1},I_{2}$ and $I_{3}$ are $4\text{A},2.5\text{A}$ and $1\text{A}$ respectively.

So current due to electrons is towards the right: $I_{e}=10^{19} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}=1.6\text{A}$ Protons have charge $+e$ and move to the left. So current due to protons is towards the left: $I_{p}=1.6\text{A}$ Alpha-particles have charge $+2e$ and move to the right. So current due to alpha-particles is towards the right: $I_{\alpha}=10^{19} \times 2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ $I_{\alpha}=3.2\text{A}$ Now take right direction as positive. $I_{\text{net}}=1.6+3.2-1.6$ $I_{\text{net}}=3.2\text{A}$ So the resulting electric current is $3.2\text{A towards right}$ Correct option: B .

Here's a representation of that setup: During the experiment, the student initially removed a resistance of $5200\Omega$ at point R. With both $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ closed and a resistance of $90\Omega$ removed at S, the galvanometer's deflection adjusted to 13 divisions. So, $AL=A^{'}L^{'}$ $A^{'}=\frac{AL}{L^{'}}=\frac{A}{1.1}$ Resistance of a wire is $R=\rho\frac{L}{A}$ New resistance will be $R^{'}=\rho\frac{L^{'}}{A^{'}}$ Substitute $L^{'}=1.1L$ and $A^{'}=\frac{A}{1.1}$ : $R^{'}=\rho\frac{1.1L}{A/1.1}=\rho\frac{1.1^{2}L}{A}=1.21R$ So resistance becomes $1.21$ times.
